title: What happens when you sleep
examples: What is the difference between light sleep and deep sleep?
Why is REM sleep important for our brains?
Does everyone go through the same sleep cycle every night?

explain.say: The sleep cycle has different stages that repeat throughout the night.
Deep sleep, or N3, is when your body does most of its physical repair work.
REM sleep is the stage where most vivid dreaming actually takes place.
The cycle moves from lighter sleep to deeper sleep and back again.
When you are studying for a test, your brain needs good sleep to remember things.
A common mistake is thinking that any sleep is equally good for your body.

faq.q: How long is one full sleep cycle?
faq.a: One full sleep cycle usually lasts about ninety minutes in total. This cycle repeats several times throughout the night.
asks: How many cycles do I get?
What is the typical length of a sleep cycle?

faq.q: Is dreaming only something that happens in REM sleep?
faq.a: While the most vivid dreams happen in REM sleep, some dreaming can occur in other stages too. The content changes as you cycle through sleep.
asks: Do I dream when I am in deep sleep?

faq.q: What is the difference between N1 and N2 sleep?
faq.a: N1 is the very beginning of sleep, a transition phase. N2 is a slightly deeper stage where your body starts to settle down more fully.
asks: Are N1 and N2 stages similar?

faq.q: Do I need different amounts of sleep depending on my age?
faq.a: Yes, different age groups need different amounts of sleep to grow and function properly. Teenagers often need more sleep than younger children.
asks: Is sleep requirements different for people?
How much sleep should I get?

faq.q: What does it mean when my body repairs itself during sleep?
faq.a: It means that your body releases hormones and energy to repair muscles and tissues. This helps you feel strong and ready for the next day.
asks: Does sleep help me get stronger?
What does the body do while I sleep?

facts: The sleep cycle repeats several times throughout a typical night.
Deep sleep is crucial for physical restoration and growth.
REM sleep is associated with vivid dreaming and memory processing.
The cycle moves through stages: N1, N2, N3, and REM.

quiz.say: Which stage is best for physical repair and growth hormone release?
quiz.why: Deep sleep is when the body focuses on physical recovery.

wrong.1: REM sleep is more focused on brain activity and dreaming.
wrong.2: N1 is just the very beginning of the sleep process.
wrong.3: Being awake means the body is not in a restorative state.

quiz.say: If you want to improve your memory, which stage is most important?
quiz.why: REM sleep is vital for processing memories and learning from the day.

wrong.1: Deep sleep helps the body, but REM helps the brain connect ideas.
wrong.2: N2 is a transition stage, not the main memory consolidation stage.
wrong.3: N1 is too light a stage to solidify new memories.

quiz.say: A full sleep cycle includes which sequence of stages?
quiz.why: This sequence shows the general progression through the main sleep stages.

wrong.0: This skips the necessary initial stages of sleep.
wrong.2: The cycle must progress from lighter to deeper sleep stages.
wrong.3: The cycle does not reverse in this specific order.
